Ahlen is part of the District of Warendorf "Warendorf (district)") and is economically the most important town in that district.*[citation needed*] Ahlen is part of the larger Münster "Münster (region)") region, and of the historic Münsterland area. The largest neighboring town is the city of Hamm to the southwest. An eel bedecked with a crown and feathers is on the town's coat of arms.

title: Louise Ahlén - Wikipedia
content: Louise Ahlén (née Holmer; 28 November 1857 – 24 May 1913) was a Swedish writer most famous for her two added verses to the Swedish National anthem.

title: Mayors of Allentown, Pennsylvania - Wikipedia
content: # Mayors of Allentown, Pennsylvania. Allentown, Pennsylvania, now the third most-populous city in Pennsylvania, was founded in 1762 as Northampton Towne by William Allen "William Allen (loyalist)"), a wealthy shipping merchant. After reaching a population of over 700 residents in the 1810 census, the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania gave Northampton Towne a legal existence on March 18, 1811, by incorporating it as the Borough of Northampton, in Northampton County. Rhodes was a prominent citizen and shopkeeper who served on the Committee of Safety "Committee of safety (American Revolution)") in Northampton Towne during the Revolutionary War. The first business of the borough government was to order cows to seek other pastures other than the public streets, an action that proved unpopular with Northampton Towne residents. The legislation was passed by the Pennsylvania Legislature on March 12, 1867, and the City of Allentown was established.
